A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LASE research, with matching authors, architecture, equations, and substantial shared experiments. The main text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-graph reconstruction, runtime, UN link-prediction, and real-network node-classification experiments, including additional classification results in Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds sensitivity analyses, graph-perturbation experiments, UN reconstruction results, and additional PowerEmbed comparisons.

M1.justification: The GD-unrolled layers, normalization, observation and attention masks, generalized-RDPG formulation, and combined reconstruction/task losses remain unchanged. Expanded training explanations and additional depth configurations do not establish a new method.

E1.justification: The original dataset families remain. v2 adds nonuniform SBM perturbations and Cora edge-addition/deletion scenarios, and directly evaluates reconstruction on the UN voting data already used for link prediction.

E2.justification: PowerEmbed newly participates in the existing UN link-prediction comparison and previously unavailable missing-edge comparisons across all four node-classification datasets, including Twitch ES. v1 supplied only cited fully observed PowerEmbed results for Cora, Amazon, and Citeseer. This substantially expands comparator coverage of the central empirical claims.

E3.justification: New settings include a Cora grid over d = {2,4,6,8,10} and L = {2,5,10,15,20}, and 20-layer, d = 4 LASE for UN reconstruction; the retained UN link-prediction model still uses 10 layers. The uniform SBM perturbation range extends from [-0.09,0.09] to [-0.09,0.10]. v2 omits the base connection matrix, leaving any change to that setting unresolved.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing robustness tests, v2 adds nonuniform SBM shifts in Figure 7, embedding-dimension/depth sensitivity in Figure 9, and Cora edge perturbations comparing single-model and multi-model training in Figure 10. These substantially broaden checks of tuning sensitivity and distribution-shift robustness.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly reports standard deviations for GD, five-step GD, and LASE reconstruction results, assessing variability from random initialization. Existing ten-trial runtime and ten-split classification reporting is retained. The reconstruction run counts are not supplied, so this does not establish an explicit increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: v2 adds UN reconstruction losses, sensitivity and perturbation results, and PowerEmbed outcomes throughout the main text and appendix. Existing values also change: Amazon LASE-5 loss moves from 453.13 to 454.23 ± 0.02, and the cited Amazon PowerEmbed accuracy from 94.6 ± 0.2 to 94.2 ± 0.2. Figure 7's uniform-shift results are replaced, but the omitted base matrix prevents assuming identical conditions. The original four-method node-classification scores otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.5 develops operation-count reasoning for convolution and masked attention, reporting total inference complexity O(L p_att N^2 d) and 2Ld^2 parameters. The earlier mathematical formulation, unrolling derivations, and Appendices A.1–A.2 remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and three principal contribution statements are essentially retained. The introduction explicitly bounds the objective as broadening ASE applicability rather than proposing a state-of-the-art positional encoding, and newly claims applicability to streaming representation tracking.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the GAT terminology as an analogy, proposes attention-graph diameter as an explanation for information propagation, and interprets PowerEmbed's strong 1980 result through its Inception component. It also interprets initialization variability and explicitly leaves broader nonspectral positional-encoding comparisons for future work.

D1.justification: v2 adds graph/noise training-pair and mini-batch training explanations, real-network edge counts, and per-year UN dataset details in Appendix A.4. Conversely, it removes the explicit SBM base matrix and replaces the direct GitHub code link with a statement about anonymized submission supplements; their availability cannot be established from these PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of subgraph encodings with Zhao et al. and Bouritsas et al., plus citations concerning Inception and change-point detection. Positioning emphasizes extending ASE applicability. The Liu-to-Cantürk citation change refers to the same Graph Positional and Structural Encoder work, rather than an added research line.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the introductory motivation, moves expressive-power background into Related Work, and introduces the UN dataset earlier in the experiments. It adds explanatory passages, acknowledgements, and two appendix subsections, while preserving the main section order and most existing exposition.

P2.justification: v2 adds the sensitivity heatmap and Cora perturbation plot, plus UN reconstruction and dataset-detail tables. Figure 7 becomes two logarithmic-axis panels, and the UN accuracy figure is redrawn with a fifth comparator. Table 1 expands to display uncertainty. Existing architecture diagrams are retained and some are relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added robustness analyses, reconstruction uncertainty, and PowerEmbed comparisons provide better support for claims that v1 tested less thoroughly. Training explanations and complexity analysis also improve transparency. These gains are tempered by unexplained revisions to cited baseline scores, inconsistent UN node totals between Tables 2 and 7, and less direct code-access instructions. The net improvement is useful but limited.
